columns.row_count: count of data rows (one per shift_id), i.e. every CSV line after the header
columns.districts: district (column 2) used as the grouping key

method.encoding: ASCII, UTF-8 compatible, LF line endings, comma delimiter, no quoted fields, no BOM
method.parsing_rule: Parse as RFC4180 CSV with a comma delimiter. Line 1 is the header and is discarded. Each subsequent non-empty line is one data row; fields are taken positionally (1=shift_id, 2=district, 3=team, 4=scheduled_hours, 5=completed_hours, 6=incidents). Numeric fields are parsed as integers; district and team as trimmed strings.
method.row_count: Number of data rows (total lines minus the 1 header line) = 6.
method.scheduled_hours: Arithmetic sum of the scheduled_hours column over all data rows = 12+8+10+14+6+9 = 59.
method.completed_hours: Arithmetic sum of the completed_hours column over all data rows = 11+8+7+13+5+9 = 53.
method.incidents: Arithmetic sum of the incidents column over all data rows = 2+1+3+0+2+1 = 9.
method.completion_percent: completed_hours / scheduled_hours * 100 = 53 / 59 * 100 = 89.83050847457627..., rounded half-up to 2 decimal places = 89.83.
method.district_grouping_rule: Group data rows by exact value of the district column (case-sensitive string). For each district emit row_count (number of rows in that group), scheduled_hours, completed_hours and incidents as ordinary sums within the group, and completion_percent = group completed_hours / group scheduled_hours * 100 rounded half-up to 2 decimal places. Districts are serialised as a JSON object keyed by district name; group totals sum exactly to the global totals (rows 2+2+2=6, scheduled 22+14+23=59, completed 18+13+22=53, incidents 5+3+1=9).
method.rounding: Percentages rounded half-up (ROUND_HALF_UP via Python decimal.Decimal.quantize('0.01')) and emitted as JSON numbers with at most 2 decimal places; counts and hours are integers.
method.cross_check: Computed three independent ways and compared to the last decimal, all in agreement: (A) python3 csv.DictReader + integer sums + decimal quantize; (B) awk -F, single-pass accumulation with associative arrays per district; (C) coreutils sort/uniq -c for district row counts plus cut|paste|bc column sums. A=(6,59,53,9,89.83), B=(6,59,53,9,89.83), C=(6 rows, 59, 53, 9) with district counts North 2 / South 2 / West 2.

notes: Header normalisation: none required. The header line 'shift_id,district,team,scheduled_hours,completed_hours,incidents' matched the expected column names exactly, with no BOM, no surrounding whitespace, no quoting and no case variation. Columns were mapped by name, with positional indices recorded above.
Trailing newline: the file ends with a single LF after the last data row; the resulting empty final element was ignored and is not counted as a data row (otherwise row_count would be 7).

Skipped malformed rows: none. Zero rows were skipped and zero rows were malformed; every one of the 6 data rows had exactly 6 fields with integer-valued scheduled_hours, completed_hours and incidents, so no row was excluded and no value was imputed or coerced.
No other cleaning, filtering, de-duplication or outlier removal was applied. Team (column 3) is present in the source but carries no required metric and is not aggregated.
The input CSV was opened read-only and was not modified; its sha256 is recorded in method.input_sha256 for reproduction.
